vocab.definition: a Group 7 non-metal with seven outer electrons.
exists as molecules of two atoms, e.g. Cl₂.
a more reactive halogen pushes out a less reactive one.
halogens gain 1 electron to form a 1− ion (halide).

misconceptions.right: They gain an electron to form 1− ions.
States change: gas → liquid → solid down the group.

questions.text: State the number of outer electrons in a halogen atom. [1 mark]
Explain why reactivity decreases down Group 7. [3 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Think about how easily the outer shell gains an electron.

questions.text: Chlorine is added to potassium bromide. Predict what happens and why. [2 marks]
Describe how a chlorine atom forms a chloride ion. [1 mark]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A halogen ______ one electron. Reactivity ______ down the group.

questions.text: Write the equation for chlorine displacing bromine from KBr. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Smaller atom → outer shell closer → gains an electron more easily → more reactive.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why can fluorine displace every other halogen?
